[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We bought this Samsung OLED TV thinking we’d just be upgrading from “pretty good” to “a bit better.” Turns out we’ve accidentally brought a cinema into the lounge room.

We’re definitely not tech experts. If the remote has more than six buttons, we start looking for the grandkids. But this TV was surprisingly easy to set up, and even we had it working without threatening to throw the instructions out the window.

The picture is incredible. The blacks are actually black instead of that washed-out grey our old TV specialised in. Colours are so sharp we’ve caught ourselves saying, “I don’t remember that actor having so many wrinkles!” Sport looks fantastic too—you can almost see the grass stains.

The sound is much better than we expected, although it still can’t drown out the neighbour mowing the lawn halfway through the footy.

The smart features are great once you remember which button gets you back to normal TV. 

Is it cheap? No. But neither are decent tyres or a good mattress, and you use this every day. We’ve got absolutely no regrets.

From two everyday Aussies who still occasionally call the remote “the clicker,” we’d happily recommend a Samsung OLED. Just be warned—you’ll spend the first week watching nature documentaries because they look so good, even if you’ve never cared about penguins before.

Five stars from us. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
review.headline: Aussie oldies review OLED smart TV

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] As the entry-level OLED in Samsung's 2026 lineup, this model doesn't come with the anti-glare coating that I am a big fan of, so it's more of a bedroom / basement TV than a bright living room TV. The upside of the lack of coating is the improved contrast and black levels, which makes a difference when you're watching night scenes in sci-fi or horror movies. 

With HDR10+ support now available across Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney Plus, Apple TV+, and Paramount+, the lack of Dolby Vision is no longer an issue. This TV brings you the best of 4K and HDR, with no compromises. The processor on this TV is also pretty good at upscaling non-4K content. 

The overall user experience is pretty smooth, and Tizen OS has gotten pretty fast and responsive. The SolarCell remote light charging is pretty useful, it's nice not worrying about charging, but I really wish that Samsung would bring back the Input button or allow for a custom button. 

You will definitely want to pair this a soundbar, ideally a Samsung one to get the most out of the center channel Q-Symphony setup, although the feet on the TV makes the placement of certain soundbars a bit more tricky if you are not wall-mounting the TV.

If you've never used an OLED before or are looking for a home theater dark room TV, the S85H is the perfect way to get started. After trying it out you will find it hard to use any other type of TV again.
review.headline: Samsung Steps Up their Entry-Level OLED Game

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] When I unboxed the Samsung S85H OLED, the first thing that stood out was just how thin it really is. After getting the correct bolts to mount it to my existing setup (M8 machine screws, 1.25"), I was able to get everything installed without issue.

I paired the TV with my new Samsung Music Studio 7 speaker, and using the Q‑Symphony feature, the TV and speaker work together to deliver really impressive sound. It’s a noticeable step up and fills the room well.

One of the biggest improvements for me has been the lack of glare. In my living room, I usually deal with reflections from daylight and overhead LED lighting, but that’s no longer an issue.

Watching during the day or at night has been a much better experience overall.

The picture quality is outstanding. The image is extremely crisp, and blacks are truly pitch black without the light bleed you typically see on more basic HDTVs. I connected both an Apple TV and a Fire TV Stick, and everything looks fantastic on this display.

I also appreciate how seamlessly the TV integrates with the Samsung SmartThings app. Having additional control and getting notifications — like alerts from the washer or dryer — is a nice bonus that fits well into my existing setup.

I would highly recommend the OLED experience to anyone who hasn’t owned one yet, especially if you’re not impressed with your current TV’s performance or struggle with glare. This TV has been a major upgrade in every way that matters to me.
review.headline: Major upgrade in every way

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This is the best TV I have owned. It has been amazing to use these past few weeks! Setup was incredibly easy using my phone, and adding all of my streaming platforms was simple -  I just scanned a QR code and confirmed the number on the screen.

The interface is also extremely fast. The wait time while navigating is practically nonexistent, which has honestly been one of my favorite features. The remote has everything I need and is clearly marked, though it took me a few tries to get used to the mute button doubling as the volume switch. I also love that the remote is rechargeable instead of constantly needing new batteries.

The smart TV features have been fun to explore. They aren’t perfect, but they’ve been exciting to try out. At first I didn’t realize I had the room detection setting turned on, so I was pleasantly surprised to be welcomed with the weather and daily stats when walking into the room. I’ve also tried the AI assistant without much luck, but because the interface itself is so quick and easy to navigate, it really hasn’t bothered me.

The TV itself is gorgeous. The screen is huge, incredibly thin, and the picture quality is honestly impressive. The colors are bright, vibrant, and super sharp across the entire screen. I’ve been shocked at the difference compared to our older TV. The speakers are also amazing and very clear, which makes movies and shows even more immersive.

It has completely transformed our family movie nights and has been such a fun product to have in our home!
review.headline: The best upgrade!

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this 65” OLED S85H 4K Samsung Vision AI TV a few weeks ago and have been really impressed overall. The brightness is excellent for an OLED panel, and HDR content looks vibrant without washing out darker scenes. Contrast is where this TV really stands out — blacks are deep and true, making movies and shows look incredibly cinematic, especially in a dark room.

The 4K resolution is super sharp, and streaming content from Netflix, YouTube, and gaming consoles looks detailed and clean. Even older content upscales surprisingly well. Viewing angles are also great since the picture quality stays consistent even when watching from the side, which is perfect for family movie nights or sports gatherings.

The refresh rate and motion handling are smooth for gaming and fast-action sports. Gameplay feels responsive with minimal blur, and movies run smoothly without noticeable stuttering. Samsung’s smart features and AI enhancements also make navigating apps and adjusting picture settings simple and quick.

What really surprised me most is the value for money. In my opinion, this TV is top of the range for the price. You get premium OLED picture quality, excellent gaming performance, smart features, and a sleek design without paying the extreme prices of some competing models.

Overall, this TV delivers premium picture quality, smooth performance, and outstanding value. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a high-end OLED TV with impressive brightness, contrast, resolution, viewing angles, refresh performance, and great bang for the buck.
review.headline: Incredible Picture and Amazing Value

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] It has been around 8 years since I updated my main living room TV. I had a 58-inch 4K TV from another brand, and I was content with it. But when I connected the Samsung OLED S85H for the first time and saw the dazzling display of colors, I felt someone had removed a filter of dullness from my eyes, and that now I was actually seeing what true colors were really like in my living room!

Now, this is not my first rodeo with OLED screens. My cellphone and PC monitor are both OLEDs. But there is a marked difference from watching an OLED screen of 7/24 inches, to one of 55! The setup went smoothly, since it was automatically detected by my Samsung phone. The smart functions of the TV have all of the streaming apps you need, and it even has XBOX Game Pass remote included, so if you have a good connection, you can actually play Game Pass games on this TV with just a controller. The TV detected my soundbar without issue, and the setup only took like 10 minutes.

The image quality of this TV is magnificent.  The blacks are real blacks, not grey like my old TV. The colors pop with dazzling brightness and contrast, and the TV has different safeguards and functions to protect the OLED display from any burn-in. I connected my game console to the TV, and gaming here is a delight as well. 

Overall, this TV showed me how much TV technology has advanced in the past few years. I now regret not getting a Samsung OLED TV sooner, since I could have been enjoying my media consumption exponentially more. But better late than never! This is the best TV I have ever owned, and I would 100% recommend it to anyone.
review.headline: OLED is a game changer!

General Review:
This ring is a really good tech device for tracking heart rate and sleep as well as exercise. You are supposed to forget about this titanium-plated ring and let it passively track your heart rate, sleep and exercise. And at only around 3 grams, it's really easy to forget about.

Battery:
I've only used this ring for a few days and over around 30 hours the battery has only depleted by 20% meaning on a full charge it will last me around a week or even more. If you wear your smartwatch while wearing this ring you can also make the battery last even more as the ring only tracks sleep and heart rate to reduce inaccuracies.

Design:
The ring has a concaved design which means that the sensors and parts of the watch would not be damaged if it has a collision with the wall or something. The cradle for the ring also looks amazing. It is like its own jewellery box for the ring itself. The ring also fits a lot better than a smartwatch and also tracks heart rate more accurately seeing as though it makes direct contact with your skin from all sides. 

Value:
It's worth it if you want a non invasive and small tech product that you want to be able to completely forget about. However if you just want your average health tracker you'd be better off going with the Samsung watch.
review.headline: Nice (fairly new) tech from Samsung

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this ring out of necessity to help me keep an track of my heart rate but also out of curiosity because I wanted to see if I will be surprised by Samsung and I must say I am stunned by the beautiful of the design of the ring and the smart charging case. Its made the ring gorgeous. 

I have worn it for over 24 hours and I hardly notice it is there because of how sleek and discrete it is but nonetheless it has made it very easy to keep track of my heart rate anytime, anywhere since I forget to put my watch on sometimes. Honestly, this has been a game changer for me and I’m sure this is going to be my number one smart gadget this year.

review.headline: Excellent health tracking wearable

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Samsung Galaxy Ring is a stylish and comfortable device. The Ring itself is made of Titanium where you have the choice of three colours, Matted Black, Silver or Gold. I opted for the Matted Black.
I would suggest when ordering your Ring to purchase the Ring Sizing Kit. This was free of charge when I ordered mine and is very helpful when choosing the right size. The presentation of the sizing ring kit appears to be very simple and sleek. When making your choice, it would be prudent to wear the Ring for a week or so, just to ensure that you have made the right decision on your chosen finger and ring size before placing your order.
The Ring itself is very well packaged similar to the Ring Sizing Kit. As you open the packaging, you are greeted with a Crystal-Clear Charging Case. As you open the case, you are again greeted with a gentle glow surrounding the Ring itself. The Case itself has several functions; short pressing the button in the middle indicates the battery level of the ring with a slight glow. If you long press the central button, this allows for Pairing Mode. The Case acts as a wireless charger for the Ring and also can be wirelessly charged itself if you have a Charging Pad.
The Ring has a sleek concave design and is very comfortable to wear. It is very light in weight to the point you can forget it is there like a standard Ring. Contained on the inside of the Ring is three sensors:
1.	Accelerometer – Tracks our Movement
2.	Optical Bio-signal Sensor - Monitors our heart rate
3.	Skin Temperature Sensor -Provides regular readings on our skin temperature changes.
In addition to the above, the Ring is waterproof. From experience of the Ring so far, I have no issues while wearing the Ring in the shower or in a swimming pool. The battery lasts between 5-7 days. The Ring is easy to connect to the Samsung Health App which provides a lot of information in terms of Sleep Tracking, Stress Levels, Step Count, BPM and also provides an Energy Score.
It is still early days but the Samsung Galaxy Ring is definitely an interesting piece of kit!
review.headline: Interesting piece of kit

The deisgn is reqlly elegant, smooth and flush it doesnt feel like you are wearing a piece off jewellery certainly not one with the amount off tech packed in it. Overall i 100% recommenend this device !!!

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Samsung Galaxy Ring looks and feels great to wear, it's light enough you don't notice it and I honestly don't know how they fit everything inside of it! The health tracking has been super accurate in my testing, and the battery life amazing compared to a smart watch.

It charges wirelessly in the provided portable case which illuminates to show the current charge status and I've been getting around 5 days battery life between charges.

Wearing it overnight is also incredibly comfortable, the Galaxy Ring tracks a lot of data while you sleep (for it's size!), including your blood oxygen, sleep stages, skin temperature, respiratory rate, and heart rate, and I love that it gives you a sleep score each night (on a 1-100 scale).

If you're looking to purchase a smart ring, you really won't regret this purchase!
review.headline: I absolutely love the Samsung Galaxy Ring!

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Galaxy Ring is a stylish, comfortable, and versatile health tracker that has exceeded my expectations. I've been impressed with its ability to accurately monitor sleep, heart rate, energy levels, steps, and more without feeling intrusive. The detailed sleep insights, including sleep stages, snoring detection, and personalized recommendations, have been especially helpful in improving my sleep quality and daytime energy.

The ring's sleek design and comfortable fit make it easy to wear all day long, even during workouts or activities. I appreciate the ability to track my progress over time and set personalized goals to stay motivated. While it may not offer the same level of detail as a smartwatch, the Galaxy Ring is a great option for those who want a discreet and effective way to track their health and fitness.

The ring is incredibly comfortable. I didn't expect this as I don't like wearing any rings at all. But I never notice this one. So sleeping with it is easy. Additionally the slight bevel makes it easy to reposition the ring without looking if it moves out of place.

It continually monitors your biostats. It is the most accurate sleep recorder I've had yet due to this. It can even alert you if your heart rate is too high or too low. I bought it specifically to get a better tracking of my periods. Previously, I only use a tracker that guesses based on previous periods. This one, however, tracks based on body temperature as well - giving a much more accurate timeframe of ovulation.

If you've got other Galaxy items, or want a start at health tracking, I'd recommend the new Galaxy Ring!

Design and weight were important for me, and the ring is amazingly light and comfortable.  I chose the silver colour as it matches my other rings. Overall, this is a great device for track, monitoring health/sleep statisctics.  There is some basic interaction, e.g. double pinch to take a photo, and assume this will get better as the software evolves.

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I want to share my excitement about the new Samsung ring. This exquisitely crafted piece of technology is surprisingly powerful, considering its small size. Upon opening the box, I was immediately struck by the beautiful presentation, which enhanced the unboxing experience. The sizing kit made it effortless to order the perfect size and I was pleasantly surprised by the impressive battery life. With just two days of use, the battery only dropped to 87%, and it recharged to 100% in just 8 minutes. The charging case is well-designed and visually appealing, with a light ring that indicates the charge level. It feels sturdy and well-constructed, almost like a work of art.

One of my key features has been using the Samsung ring while sleeping. It blends seamlessly into my night time routine, providing perfect and comfortable sleep tracking, which is non-intrusive. The morning after, my Z Fold 6 delivered a comprehensive analysis of my sleep pattern, detailing everything from my sleep and wake-up times to my physical and mental recovery. It even tracked my heart rate, temperature, and different sleep stages.

I eagerly look forward to putting the ring to the test with physical activities to see how well it can track them.
review.headline: Beautiful and full of technology

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First, the size is not a normal ring size due to the sensors, so make sure to use the sizing kit or order a size bigger.
If you are a Samsung user, it will work and pair flawlessly. It integrates directly with Wear and Health. I find the form factor of a ring great for getting the extra data, amazing for me as I don’t want notifications, just the health data points during the day and when sleeping. This has been great during my first 48 hours with the ring.
The size and technology are truly outstanding. Also, the battery life looks to be in line withh the promised seven-day battery life. The charging case is also a nice touch, with the ring around the case showing charge levels and when charging is complete. The case is USB-C and Qi compatible and can itself charge the ring a couple of times.
The device, tested in water, in the shower and the Center Parcs pool, has not missed a beat and provides heart rate data even when going down the rapids!
The only letdown so far is the black paint; my ring appears to be chipping already, which raises significant concerns about how long this version will retain its attractive appearance.
I can reconditioned the ring to Samsung users after health data without a watch, but with a warning that the black version maybe not be the best bet if you want ot as a fashion statement long term.
review.headline: Form factor & tech, just not is stay looking nice

review.reviewBody: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Health monitoring it is great and gives a real thorough insight into sleep and rest patterns. However for texting fitness it is terrible, I ran several times with it with a GPS Garmin watch which showed 5k and the ring said I had ran 4.2k. I then wore my galaxy watch on the same run and even though it had the same steps as the ring, the ring once again inaccurately said 4.2k. My step count is also massively out on the ring despite all my credentials remaining accurate. Disappointing as I want to ditch wearing a watch for fitness/step and sleep tracking.
review.headline: Disappointing. Runs & Steps out by 20%

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] If you are looking for something different, smart and effective then look no further than the Galaxy Ring from Samsung. 

A ring testing kit delivered in a slick black box followed by the product in an equally stunning presentation case was exactly what I expected from a high value premium product. 

Not a lover of wearing a watch to bed but interested in my sleep patterns and health, this does it in an extremely comfortable way. The data collected via the app is amazing and interesting and displayed in a very understandable way. It brings a sense of excitement in the mornings to see how my night had been and in comparison, to previous. The app gives as much as the product itself.

I opted for the Black version, and I am not disappointed. It is durable, scratch resistant and easy to setup and use. The battery life is fantastic and having a charging station/dock provided makes this an item that can be taken everywhere.

The light sensors are raised towards the inside of the ring and take a little getting used too. However, in lowlight you can see them clearly working and measuring data and lighting up the base of the finger. 

The Ring has been beautifully designed, and the performance of the smart aspect is much better than I original thought and gave credit for. I would recommend this to others that have a Samsung Smart Phone as the interaction between the 2 devices is seamless!
review.headline: Galaxy Ring from Samsung

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I received my smart ring and upon opening the box, you see the ring inside the elegant charging case, it arrived fully charged and upon opening the charger and removing the ring, I automatically got a message on my phone to add my ring, within around a minute, it was synced and working, I'm amazed by the power, spec and battery of the ring considering its size. After 1.5 days, I suspect the battery will last over 6 days, this will be extended when wearing with my Galaxy watch apparently, but I wanted to test the ring without the watch to start with as I know some features of the ring and watch get disabled to preserve the battery of both devices.

The main reason I wanted the smart ring was because I've always disliked wearing my smartwatch in bed as its not comfortable, however, I find the ring comfortable and now have all the same stats I had before. I also find the blood o2 sensor is more stable, as before my watch was always too tight, or moved in my sleep and didn't record fully, I no longer have that problem.

My steps seem to be accurate and I'm looking forward to trying with more physical activities to see how this effects my energy score

There are features that aren't enabled yet, but Samsung say they are coming soon. These include taking photos or snooze alarm clocks by pinching my fingers

All in all I'm extremely happy with my purchase and looking forward to the added features coming soon.
review.headline: Smart Ring

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] One of the standout features of the Galaxy Ring is its sleek and minimalist design. It's incredibly comfortable to wear, even during sleep, thanks to its lightweight construction and smooth finish. The ring's unobtrusive size and design make it a discreet way to monitor your health and fitness.
In terms of functionality, the Galaxy Ring offers a solid range of features. Its sleep tracking capabilities are particularly impressive, providing detailed insights into your sleep quality, including REM sleep, light sleep, and deep sleep. The ring also accurately tracks your heart rate, steps, and calories burned throughout the day.

However, there are a few areas where the Galaxy Ring could improve. While its health tracking features are reliable, it may not be as comprehensive as some other smartwatches or fitness trackers on the market. Additionally, the battery life could be better, although it generally lasts for several days on a single charge.

Overall, the Galaxy Ring is a promising first-generation smart ring. Its comfortable design, accurate health tracking, and seamless integration with the Samsung ecosystem make it a compelling option for those looking to monitor their health and fitness in a discreet and convenient way.
I have shown this to most of my patients and had been useful to use in some cases with logged sleep patterns and forward fitness monitoring. I will continue to see how well this benefits in the long run.
review.headline: One ring to rule them all?

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I have been waiting for the Samsung Ring for a while!

I love the presentation box, the clear charging case and of course the ring itself. The brushed titanium silver is beautiful. The ring is incredibly lightweight, and the sizing is perfect. I wore the sizing ring for over 3 days to ensure the fit was going to be right, and I am glad it is. The ring feels natural and comfortable to wear all day. It is durable and hard-wearing, waterproof and easy to clean. It does capture fingerprints, but a quick wipe and it is good.

I have a Samsung phone so the pairing was very simple. The ring was detected instantly by the Wearable app and was set up ready to go within a few minutes. My health data and targets etc were synced too. Having Samsung products already makes a huge difference as they all talk to each other within the ecosystem. My phone, watch and ring are all in sync and work together seamlessly.

The ring is intuitive and has measured heart rate and workouts very well. The sleep measurements on snoring and blood oxygen is very insightful and I am looking forward to a fuller picture in the next few weeks. I like looking at the energy score and hope future updates capture more health data and workouts.

I have had it for over 24 hours and the battery life seems to be great so far. The case itself carries charge so doesn’t need to be plugged in for over two weeks!

I am pleased with the ring and I am sure it will get better with future software upgrades.
review.headline: Great start, will get better

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Was so excited to try this ring and couldn't wait for it to arrive .I would definitely recommend getting the ring sizer to ensure you order the right size. Even so the ring was much tighter when it arrived then the ring sizer was on my finger. I would also say the sizes are limited and not made for people with larger fingers.
It has a good price point compared to other similar smart rings as there is no monthly fee.
I was very impressed with the look of the ring. I got the Titanium silver one. I was quite surprised at how flimsy and light it was when I picked it up and very plasticky.
It is very easy to wear and looks good on my finger.
It tracks health and wellbeing although is quite limited on which workouts it can track compared to other smart rings. The best part of the ring is the sleep tracker. Each morning, the Ring feeds information about your previous day to the App, which gives you an Energy Score comprised of the following factors: Sleep time average, Sleep time consistency, Bed/wake time consistency, Sleep timing, Previous day activity, Sleeping heart rate, and Sleeping heart rate variability, or HRV. 
 It gives you lots of useful information and also there is a temperature tracker and it tracks runs and walks. It also provides well being tips based on your data.
It is a shame that it is only compatible with Android phones and this may put come people of buying it.
Hopefully in future there will be software updates to enable more people to use it.
review.headline: Fabulous Health and sleep tracker

review.reviewBody: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Galaxy Ring is Samsung's latest venture into wearable tech, and after a week of use, I’m impressed with this smart ring.Design: Its understated elegance really stands out. The ring is so lightweight and comfortable that I often forget I'm wearing it. Unlike bulky smartwatches, it’s easy to wear all day and night.Functionality: The ring excels at health and sleep tracking, offering detailed insights into sleep patterns, heart rate, and activity levels. The personalized sleep feedback is especially useful, and the fun feature that compares your sleep to an animal is a nice touch. When paired with a Samsung watch, it provides even more comprehensive health data.Battery Life: The battery life is impressive, lasting a full seven days on a single charge. This is much better than many other wearables that need daily charging. The clear charging case is a nice addition, giving the whole experience a bit of a premium feel.Areas for Improvement: There are a few areas where the Galaxy Ring could be better. It’s missing NFC for contactless payments, which is a bit of a letdown, and the software could use a few more features to make it even more versatile.Overall: The Galaxy Ring is a great choice for anyone looking for a sleek, comfortable, and effective health tracker. It fits seamlessly into your daily routine, offering useful feedback and helping promote healthier habits. Despite a few minor drawbacks, I a highly recommended this piece of tech that lives up to its promises.
review.headline: A Sleek and Insightful Health Companion

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been hesitant to pick up a smart ring but when Samsung announced their ring I knew I had to take a shot at it. Having access to their ecosystem and tying all my devices together is a great selling point and the ring works out of the box with their watches to provide a seamless experience. 

Battery life is great, easily lasting several days and when it does come time to charge it, just throw it in the charging case for an hour or so and your good again for another week. Luckily if you have also purchased their Watch, you won't lose tracking whilst it's charging since the watch and Ring work together in tandem. 

The health tracking looks great too. Able to track your sleep, heart rate, skin temperature and other things too. The sleep reports are detailed, and provide easy access to analytics showing you where your lacking and need to improve. It's also allows you to track your average heart rate whilst sleeping.

Improvement wise, I'd like to see blood pressure monitoring included. This is a feature that appears to be coming to some other competitor devices, but I get that Samsung needed to deliver a solid offering here for their first attempt and that future versions could introduce additional features like this. Same goes for NFC payments, it would be very useful to be able to pay for things with the ring. 

Overall this is a solid effort from Samsung and a great first attempt to get into the smart ring market. Like their other devices, I expect they will quickly innovate and then refine their rings over the next few years.
review.headline: Stylish and comfortable

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The sizing kit that arrived prior to the ring being delivered was super useful in choosing the correct size of ring since the sensors make sizing slightly different to regular rings.
The instructional video for sizing was simple and easy to follow! 
After 24 hours of testing (as ring size changes between day/night and at different temperatures) I was confident of my ring size and confirmed it on my order.

The ring itself has a beautiful sleek design and doesn’t clash with other pieces of jewellery. 
The reason why I bought the ring was to get the same benefits of health tracking that you’d get with a smart watch without constantly feeling that it’s there and the Samsung ring absolutely achieves this. 
I barely noticed that I was wearing the ring as it’s really lightweight and comfortable to wear.

The battery life is great as it has only depleted by a few percent after just over a day of use so I’m sure the ring would stay charged for well over a week. 

In regard to tracking, the insight that the ring provides in terms of sleep quality and exercise is good.  
After analysing my sleep patterns and sleep score, I realised that my sleep is more interrupted than I thought it was so will be making changes to help with that. 
The ring recorded my workout pretty well so I had an accurate measure of my heart rate throughout, exercise time and approximately how many calories I burned.

I think I’ve finally found my perfect health and fitness companion and I’m super excited to test the ring out more and get properly acquainted with all its features!
review.headline: Samsung Ring

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Samsung ring has surprised me and is one of my favourite gadgets. It's comfortable to wear and looks and feels durable. The battery lasts for quite a few days, and you can easily check it by placing it back in its case.
The ring syncs with the Health app without flaw and uploads the data to the phone. It has taken me some time to get familiar with the app, but after a few days, I have familiarised myself with most of the features but I am still learning.
During the day, it tracks steps and calculates activity time, beats per minute, stress level and oxygen levels, although I'm not really sure how accurate the stress indicator is. The app gives supportive notifications once you have reached your daily goals, steps, calories and minutes and prompts you to move if you have been inactive for too long. You can record workouts like walking and running and more, and it gives a lot of information about them; here I may be missing a graph of the heart rate, but still, there is a lot of data.
It has a great section about sleeping. It calculates a sleeping score and shows the different stages of my sleep: deep, REM, and light. It also shows graphs with oxygen levels and beats per minute across the night. The graphs look a bit small on my phone. Snoring detection is not activated by default, and you need to have your phone nearby to detect it when sleeping. You can also compare and check the data from previous days.
Overall, I think it is a great device. It has exceeded my expectations regarding the data that it tracks. The learning curve of the app has been a bit steeper than I initially anticipated but worth the time to understand better my sleep habits and physical activity.
review.headline: Very impressed

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve been interested in purchasing a smart ring for some time – I like to “bling up” my wrists with jewellery, and I always find a smart watch to be somewhat obvious and intrusive. My ring sits comfortably and discreetly on either my index finger or ring finger constantly recording a good deal of information. As a piece of jewellery, it is fairly non-descript, it is plastic, coloured to look like various metals. I’d like to see them embrace the “plastic” and perhaps offer some funky colours, or pearlized finish, rather than trying to pretend it is metal. That said, my colleagues at work commented on how robust it looked, and were genuinely surprised when I said it was plastic.
It comes in a great little charging case, which sits by the side of my bed. The charging case looks expensive, and will ensure that I won’t lose my ring when charging it! It’s also great for travelling, ensuring my ring is always protected when not on my finger. The battery holds a decent charge, and I get about 7 days before I’m reminded by my phone that my ring needs charging.
Set up was super easy! I took it out the box, my phone beside me, and it connected immediately without me actually having to do anything!
The data it collected is very insightful, helping me with my weight loss programme. It tracks your activities, monitors heart rate, calories burned and gives a good insight into your sleeping habits, including recording your snoring habits, much to my amusement! The app is intuitive to use and it’s easy to track improvements in your health.
Having used the ring for about two weeks now, I’d definitely recommend this as a fitness tracker, but I would like to see some creativity in the plastic body of the ring.
review.headline: Discreet Fitness Tracking

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've had the Galaxy Ring for about 3 days now, and I'm quite pleased with it overall. The only downside I found is the sizing; I had to order a Size 13 ring (the largest size available), which just about fits on my small finger - on the positive side, this does provide longer battery life.
The free sizing kit, which I highly recommend using, helped me choose the correct size. Upon receiving the ring, I was delighted by the elegant black box and modern charging case. I chose a black ring. The black ring's sleek and stylish design is something I appreciate, as it isn't overly flashy and complements my style. 
Pairing the ring with my S24 took just a few seconds through the Wearable app. The seamless health tracking integration with my phone, watch, and ring has been impressive. The ring's lightweight nature makes it comfortable for wearing all-day and all-night, and its battery life appears to be excellent, likely lasting at least 8 days before requiring a recharge.
Tracking health metrics with the Galaxy Ring has been insightful. The sleep measurements provide a comprehensive view of my sleep quality, which is especially useful as I suffer with Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnoea. I used to rely on my Galaxy Watch for tracking my sleep, now I can put the watch on charge and use my Galaxy Ring.
The Galaxy Ring is proving to be a fantastic health and fitness companion. Its stylish design, ease of use, and seamless integration with the Samsung ecosystem make it a worthwhile investment for anyone interested in tracking their health and wellbeing. Despite the sizing issue, I am very pleased with my purchase and highly recommend it to anyone looking for an alternative to a smartwatch for health tracking.
review.headline: Stylish with Health Insights

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upon ordering the ring, I was presented with the dilemma of which ring size to choose. Fortunately, Samsung appreciate that you need to get this right and give you the option to receive a ring sizing kit prior to choosing the actual ring size you want. This came through very quickly and comes in a box with nine different sizes to try on. This ensures you can pick the right ring for the right finger and is a great idea. 

Upon receiving the actual ring i was impressed by the charging case it comes in which feels premium. The ring upon first putting it on felt a little bulky and definitely took some getting used to despite having already had a trial with the dummy rings. However, after 24 hours of wearing the ring it has already got to the point where I forget it is there similar to my wedding ring. 

The main benefit that I was looking forward to with the ring was finally being able to track my sleep at night which I had never been able to achieve with a watch. The ring tracks multiple different criteria such as your sleep stages, your blood oxygen and your skin temperature. It even can track when you snore and much to my embarrassment get your phone to record the audio so you can play it back to hear exactly what you sound like!

The battery on the ring is very long lasting. Upon receiving the ring it had 80% battery. A week later and without having yet charged it, the battery remains at 26% charge. This is despite wearing it at all times, visiting the gym twice, going on multiple dog walks a day and then normal every day activities in between.  

Overall the ring achieves what it sets out to do which is be a discrete smart tracker and it does this well. Given that this item is new I am sure there will be further updates to the software to bring even more features to the ring. I am glad I made the purchase.
review.headline: Great Discrete Smart Tracker Ring

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Having recently purchased the Samsung Galaxy Ring, I can confidently say that I absolutely love it. As someone who has struggled to sleep comfortably with a smartwatch, finding a device that prioritizes sleep tracking was crucial for me. The Galaxy Ring has proven to be the perfect solution, seamlessly integrating with my Galaxy Watch for enhanced health monitoring.

Key Features

Comfort and Design: The Galaxy Ring is incredibly lightweight and unobtrusive, making it easy to wear throughout the day and night. Unlike bulkier smartwatches, it feels almost unnoticeable, allowing for a comfortable sleep experience. The sleek design and various size options ensure a good fit for everyone.

Comprehensive Health Tracking: This ring excels in providing detailed health metrics, including heart rate, SPO2 levels, temperature, and sleep tracking. The combination of these features gives a holistic view of daily activity and health, which is invaluable for anyone serious about their wellness.

Battery Life: After using the ring since Monday, I still have 74% battery remaining, which is impressive. The battery life is estimated to last up to seven days on a single charge, making it convenient for continuous wear without frequent recharging.

No Subscription Required
One of the standout aspects of the Galaxy Ring is that it does not require a subscription to access its features, unlike competitors like the Oura Ring. This makes it a more appealing option for those looking to track their health without ongoing costs.

Conclusion
In summary, if you're in the market for a discreet and effective health tracker that provides comprehensive metrics without the bulk of a smartwatch, the Samsung Galaxy Ring is an excellent choice. Its combination of comfort, functionality, and affordability makes it a standout in the wearable tech space.
review.headline: A Game-Changer for Sleep and Health Tracking

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This small but mighty smart ring keeps track of your health and sleep as well as many other features. It is available in 3 colours - black, silver and gold. 

I decided to get the free ring sizing kit to help confirm what ring size I needed. These rings are a plastic replica of the galaxy ring. They came promptly in the mail and neatly packaged. I was able to try the various size rings to determine what size of galaxy ring I needed and which finger I preferred to wear it on. Once I had worn the sizing ring for 24 hours as Samsung suggest I went online and ordered my correct size knowing it was going to be the right size and comfortable to wear whilst doing my usual tasks.

The Galaxy Ring arrived a couple of days later and I was very excited to start wearing my new piece of tech. I opened the box to find it in all its glory inside and neatly packaged charging case. It looks so beautiful in its charging case, an ingenious design by Samsung. 

Once I opened the charging case it easily synced with my Samsung phone and was able to start the software download and in less than a minute it was ready to wear.  If your phone doesn't detect the ring, put ion back in it's charger and press the button in the case for 3 seconds and your phone with connect. Super simple and easy to connect and set up, another great quality about Samsung. 

I've been wearing the ring since it arrived. I have to say I'm very impressed with the ring, the design, colour and stylishness. It is super comfortable to wear throughout the day and during sleep. I'm also impressed that the galaxy watch and ring will disable features to preserve the battery life between the devices extending the health data your receive on your phone. I can't wait for the new added features coming soon for the ring. 

The ring is great for anyone looking to improve their health and for any tech head like myself. Samsung have provided an excellent device yet again. I'm very pleased with my purchase and I'd definitely recommend.
review.headline: Mighty Smart Ring

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I'm really pleased with my Samsung Ring. It's a sleek, lightweight ring that fits comfortably. Sometimes, I even forget I'm wearing it. As a woman, I was a bit worried that it might be designed with men in mind, but the band looks feminine enough on my skinny fingers. While a thinner band would be an excellent choice, I'm happy with how this one looks.

I chose the Samsung Ring because I like smartwatches, but I dislike the daily charging, sleeping with a watch on, and the constant vibrations and alerts. I'm still interested in tracking my wellness and sleep patterns. The ring allows me to wear jewellery and traditional watches with less maintenance.

I used the sizing kit before ordering the ring, and I'm glad I did because I changed my mind about which finger felt the most comfortable. I ended up choosing my middle finger over my index finger. I was between sizes 8 and 9 but chose the smaller size for a better fit. The samples are true to size, but the actual ring is even more comfortable.


The ring features health tracking, including activity, heart rate monitoring, sleep tracking, cycle tracking, and blood oxygen level monitoring, all synced with the Samsung Health app. The best part is that I get all this data from such a tiny product, without any added subscription costs, and the battery lasts several days on a single charge. It pairs seamlessly with Samsung devices, offering intuitive app integration.

Pros:
- Stylish and comfortable
- Comprehensive health tracking
- Long battery life

Cons:
- Lack of contactless payments feature
- Limited display interaction

Conclusion:
I highly recommend the Samsung Ring for making my life easier, and blends style with functionality, making it ideal for Samsung users seeking a fashionable tech accessory. Despite the premium price, it offers excellent features and convenience, providing a breath of fresh air in the oversaturated smartwatch market. The ring is still in its early days of development, with many more features and functionalities to be developed.
review.headline: Style with functionality

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Samsung's entry into the smart ring market has been long awaited and I was thrilled to finally get to try it out.

The sizing process for the Galaxy Smart Ring was handled well - a small box with plastic replica rings from sizes 5-13. I tried on a few sizes and on different fingers before settling for the one that fit comfortably both day and night. I did the sizing before ordering my ring, but you can also get a sizing kit as part of your order and they will ship the ring with your chosen size.

Unboxing is always fun, and I love the case that the Galaxy Ring comes in. This doubles as a charging cradle and on the go charger for the ring, due to its built in battery. 
It's still early days with regard to testing battery life, but it is rated for up to 7 days on a full charge. I'm one day since a full charge showing 87% remaining, so that's within the expected range.

The ring is comfortable to wear (helped by choosing the right size before ordering!) and looks quite nice - not too thick or conspicuous, which is what I wanted. 

The main features are of course the health information that is tracked by the ring - primarily activity, heart rate and sleep. 
Sleep tracking seems to be quite accurate, although I'll need to track it over a longer period to get some practical insights.
Heart rate tracking is displayed in graphs with Min/Max per hour as well as a rolling daily resting average.
This is all tied together through an "Energy Score" which takes in all of the tracked metrics and gives suggestions based on this (e.g. "Don't overdo it!" which I received the day after a long run). This also highlights areas that require attention (sleep, recent activity etc)

Unfortunately some of the gesture features that I have looked forward to (tap index finger and thumb together to take photo or cancel an alarm) are not yet supported on my Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra phone, but this is expected to be added in the next software update (One UI 6.1.1 ).

So far I'm really impressed by the ring and am looking forward to getting some more insights into my current sleep and activity habits. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who likes to track these sorts of things, but perhaps doesn't want to wear a smart watch all of the time.
review.headline: The next generation of health tracking

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I think for a smart ring, this is a great piece of kit. It feels really comfortable on and syncs in seconds with my samsung phone. The charging case is a proper touch, so simple to keep it by the bed and even carry around for it to charge when it's out of battery.

It may be unfair to give it 4 out of 5, because my odd rationale is that it's not as smart as a smart watch and perhaps I expected it to do more, even though it does exactly what it says on the tin - I am just glad not to have to charge something every couple days.
review.headline: easy, long lasting fitness and sleep tracker

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Being an Samsung Android user it's been great to get the Samsung ring.  My main use case was to provide a view into sleep anbd step tracking, without having to accept wearing a big smart watch 24/7.

The ring form factor works brilliantly for this and is a much more convenient way to constantly generate this insight in a subtle way.

The ring sizing approach from Samsung was excellent and I definitely recommend grabbing the free ring sizing kit.  I ended up with a size 12 worn on my middle finger after expecting to use a smaller size on a ring finger so the chance to trial was valuable.

Unboxing experience was positive and the supplied charger case felt premium and will be useful on longer trips to easily recharge the ring.  This won't be often however as battery life has proved to be excellent, usually lasting 6+ days between charges with all tracking options activated (aside form snore tracking!).

The ring itself is very light and comfortable with an understated design.  It also appears to be pretty robust with no sign of wear after nearly a months solid use 24/7.

Sleep tracking, my main interest from the ring, appears to work well with some interesting insights in the Samsung health app.  I'm not sure how much "use" some of the details about blood oxygen and skin temperature are, but they are interesting to look through. 
 There has also been a good correlation between nights where I have not slept well and woke up feeling groggy with the ring showing issues in my sleep (awake time, not enough deep sleep etc).  More than anything though I've definitely found that since having the ring I am more conscious of trying to get good quality sleep.

Step and activity tracking is super handy to be able to track all the time without needing to wear other devices like a watch.  One small issue is that I'm not yet convinced though that the workout tracking works perfectly.  I have not always seen "walking" workouts be auto-detected reliably.  

Finally in the last couple of days the software upgrade has enabled gesture control on my Samsung Ultra S24.  While it only supports alarm cancellation and taking a picture, these are suprisingly convenient.

Overall, it's a good device in an excellent form factor and offers an interesting insight into sleep and activity.  I'm not sure it's something to use though, if perfect activity tracking accuracy is what you need.
review.headline: Handy solution for sleep and fitness tracking

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] As a diabetic, monitoring my health has become an important part of my daily routine. My smart watch has been invaluable for this but I don’t always remember to charge my watch and I don’t like wearing it when I sleep. A smart ring therefore seemed like a great alternative.

When ordering you have the option to buy a sizing kit comprising a number of plastic rings so you can determine what will fit you best and which finger you want to wear it on (it does recommend using your index finger for gesture control functions but it will work on any finger or thumb). I strongly recommend doing this as the sizing system wasn’t one I was familiar with and the sensors on the inside of the ring may affect the fit. 

Once you’ve worked out what fits you best, you confirm the size and await delivery. The ring arrives in a gorgeous clear charging case that has an LED ring around the centre displaying how much charge the case has left in it or how much charge the ring has when it’s placed in the case. The case supports wireless charging or USB C, handy if you need to use your phone to reverse wireless charge.

You use Samsung Health and Wearable to interact with the ring and access the data it tracks, such as heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep analysis etc as well as setting alerts reminding you to move, drink water or if your heart rate goes above or below a specified level. If you’re managing a diet you can also use the app to record what you’re eating too which is quite useful. 

The ring automatically detects walking and running and proved very good at recognising when I broke into jog while walking. It can track other activities too but these need to be manually selected from the phone app. The real stand out for me though was the sleep analysis – it gave me an incredibly detailed breakdown of the different phases of sleep, my skin temperature during sleep (which helped me to spot what was waking me up) and it provides tips for getting better rest. 

Battery-wise I comfortably got to the end of 6 days before it hit 20% and I felt the need to top it up.

Overall, it’s an incredibly easy device to integrate into your daily routine and you can happily put it on and just let it do its thing. I’d like to see a little more functionality and I look forward to trying out gesture control when my S23 Ultra receives the appropriate update but in the meantime it's a useful tool when you're managing your weight or living with certain conditions.
review.headline: Stylish innovation

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] There's a lot of competition in the smart ring market these days, and I was concerned that Samsung's attempt would be met with turbulence. However, I'm happy to say I think they've done a fantastic job.

I opted for the matte black ring, and after wearing the sizing kit for a few days chose a size 9 for my finger. The ring itself is much more comfortable than the sizing kit, so don't let that put you off if you choose to check your size first. The packaging is very on brand for Samsung - minimalistic, functional and timeless. The box that houses the ring itself is almost like a wedding ring box, as you open it upwards to reveal the ring inside the charging case. Everything you need is in the box (excluding a mains adapter, so you'll need a USB-C plug on hand).

The charging case has some weight to it, which adds to it's premium design and feel. The hinge for the lid is smooth and tactile, which feels great to use. Once open you're met with a ring of light which shows the charge percentage of the case. When placing the ring on in the case it will show the charge percentage of the ring before fading out. I've not tested the actual capacity of the charging case, but it is stated to hold 1.5 times the charge of the ring.

The ring itself is incredibly light, surprisingly so in fact. The material doesn't feel like titanium, or metal at all actually, but this is due to the scratch resistant coating that Samsung have applied. I absolutely forget it's on my finger sometime, which is surprising because of the sensors mounted to the inside of the ring (not to mention a battery too).

My Samsung S34 Ultra detected the ring instantly, and within seconds I was connected and being taken through the basic info of the ring. So far it's been very interesting, and while coupled with a Samsung watch the pair communicate to give you accurate and up to date readings. My first night sleep with the ring was my biggest highlight though, as it tracked my heartrate, blood oxygen, body temperature and sleep quality; wrapping everything up in a sleep score. It told me what type of sleep I had and what the benefits of each were (light, heavy, REM). And I think the cherry on top is that there is no subscription fee for this, setting it apart from the competition.

Overall I think Samsung have done a great job with the ring. It's missing some gestures that were advertised (coming soon to UK), and some types of sensor readings. But all in all I'm very impressed!

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This Samsung Ring is such a game changer in the whole health tracking industry.
It is amazing at helping you regulate your sleep according to the coach's instructions.
Every morning, you can check the parameters of the previous night and receive instructions from the coach on how to improve your sleep results. Also, worth to mention - it tracks your oxygen levels throughout the night. I think, it's a great device, to check if you have undiagnosed sleep apnea.

By setting a continuous heart rate measurement, we get the full day tracking and accurate results. By clicking on the hourly measurement interval in the app, we can see the results, even what the pulse was in a certain minute interval.

The Samsung Ring is incredible during workouts and simple walks. When walking faster, you can see how the heart worked and how long it worked in different modes based on the size of the pulse.

review.reviewBody:

Its comfortable design makes it easy to wear throughout the day and night, while the long battery life means you don't have to constantly worry about charging it. The biggest downside is that some of its features are most useful when paired with a Samsung Galaxy smartphone.

Overall: The Galaxy Ring is a stylish, discreet, and convenient wearable for anyone who wants health tracking without wearing a smartwatch. It may be small, but it delivers a surprisingly complete experience.
review.headline: Galaxy Ring

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Samsung Galaxy Ring is an impressive piece of wearable tech that seamlessly combines style and functionality. From accurate health tracking to smart notifications, it covers all the essentials you’d expect from a modern wearable. The sleek design is comfortable, making it easy to wear throughout the day without feeling bulky.

One standout feature is its detailed health monitoring. The ring tracks everything from heart rate to sleep patterns, offering insights that are genuinely useful for anyone looking to stay on top of their wellness. The battery life is also commendable, lasting several days on a single charge, which is a big plus for those who don’t want to worry about frequent recharging.

The only drawback I've noticed is that the ring scratches quite easily. Despite being careful, I’ve found a few nicks on the surface after just a few weeks of use. It’s a minor issue, but if you're particular about keeping your gadgets pristine, it’s something to consider.

Overall, the Samsung Galaxy Ring is a fantastic choice for anyone in the market for a smart ring. It does everything you’d expect and more, with the only downside being its tendency to pick up scratches. If you can overlook that, you’ll find it to be a valuable addition to your tech collection.
review.headline: Impressive Features, but Scratches Easily

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve been using the Samsung Galaxy Smart Ring, and overall, it’s been a great experience. The ring is incredibly lightweight and discreet, looking just like a normal ring, which I love. However, it does feel a bit cheap at times, almost plasticky, even though it’s not actually made of plastic.

During my recent holidays, I really put it to the test. I wore it in swimming pools and the ocean, and it held up well under these conditions. There are some small scratches on the underside, probably from my more extreme testing, but overall, it’s been quite durable. 

One of the standout features is the battery life, which is excellent. The most impressive aspect, though, is the sleep tracking. Wearing a watch to bed isn’t ideal, but the ring is perfect. It’s comfortable to wear at night and provides detailed insights into my sleep patterns, along with step tracking throughout the day.

The data from the ring has definitely influenced my habits. I’ve found myself going to bed earlier, and when I get good sleep, it reflects in how I feel the next day. The app’s affirmations of my sleep quality are spot-on, whether I’ve had a restful night or a restless one.

Overall, the Samsung Galaxy Smart Ring has been a reliable and helpful tool in monitoring my sleep and activity, despite some minor flaws in the build quality.

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First of all, I’ve always loved the idea of a ring-based fitness tracker and the benefits it can provide and the Galaxy Ring certainly doesn’t disappoint. What I would say is that it’s definitely worth trying the sizing kit before you select your actual ring to get the best fit possible for the finger you intend to wear it on. I ended up with the largest size (13) and it fits perfectly.
Having used the ring there are a lot of positives The first is how discreet it is, I always forget I'm wearing it even to the point it's almost run out of charge before I've realised and when wearing it at night for sleep tracking it is practically un-noticeable. The design of the ring and particularly the charging case are excellent and look incredibly smart, especially the light which shows how much charge is remaining when you open it.
The actual sensors provide all the major measurements you’re likely to need HR, step count skin temperature etc and it integrates seamlessly into the Samsung Health App.
The only other thing I would have like to see was Samsung Pay technology to have been included, so you wouldn't need to take any other device / cards with you when you went out. However, considering how much amazing technology they have crammed in to something so small then I doubt there's room for anything else. 
Having said that, I do really enjoy the Ring and the benefits it provides. I'd definitely recommend it to anyone thinking of trying out a fitness tracker.

review.headline: Love the Galaxy Ring

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Having used the Samsung Galaxy Watch for some time, I found it uncomfortable to wear at night, which meant I wasn’t able to track my sleep effectively. The **Samsung Galaxy Ring** has filled that gap perfectly.

**Fit and Comfort**

The Ring's **sizing kit** is crucial for ensuring a good fit. I recommend testing all your fingers in different climates, as slight changes in temperature can affect finger size and comfort. A well-fitted ring is essential for both comfort and accurate data collection. However, my only gripe is the contoured design, which can sometimes dig into adjacent fingers. A traditional ring design might have offered a more comfortable fit without compromising the look.

**Battery Life**

The **battery life** is outstanding. Unlike many wearables that require frequent charging, the Galaxy Ring lasts several days on a single charge, making it extremely convenient and hassle-free for continuous use.

**Experience and Features**

The overall experience with the Galaxy Ring has been excellent. The **sleep tracking** feature has been a game-changer for me, allowing me to make conscious changes to my sleep habits and daily routine. The detailed insights into my sleep patterns have helped improve my overall well-being, as I've been able to adjust my bedtime and optimize my sleep environment based on the data provided.

**Conclusion**

Despite my minor issue with the contoured design, the Samsung Galaxy Ring is a fantastic product that has exceeded my expectations. It offers an effective and comfortable solution for sleep tracking, making it a worthwhile investment for anyone looking to gain better insights into their sleep and health.
review.headline: Samsung Galaxy Ring Review

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Having tried this ring out for a week, while also only a family trip to Brighton, I can confidently say I love it. 

The ring is discreet which is such a welcomed change from the bulkiness of smart watches. You don't notice it while out and about, working out and most importantly while asleep! Watches are a pain to wear while sleeping in particular so this is a great alternative if you are interested in tracking your sleep primarily.

Durability is great - this ring survived 3 days on Brighton beach and came out without a scratch even though I was playing with sand and stones with the little ones.

Battery life is amazing - I put it on on Tuesday and it lasted till the following Monday, all while tracking sleep and steps (and while travelling). This is a Size 9 ring, so those opting for a bigger size will get an even better battery life.

Health tracking is useful, I use it mostly to analyse my sleep and energy score, although the step tracking is a neat feature. Not needing a subscription is a great perk. The app UI is also intuitive although there should be more options to customise notifications eg I get daily goal alerts, which I don't want, but need to switch off all notifications to stop this.

Overall this is a great device for those who are focused on tracking sleep, steps and health scores passively (all information is visible on your phone app rather than on the wearable). For those who want to actively interact with a wearable device and want more detailed live fitness tracking, I think a watch would be better. Going forward I think a combination of both is the ideal use case for me - the ring for 24/7 tracking while the watch for fitness tracking.

Well done Samsung on a solid 1st gen Ring!

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Overall I am fairly impressed with the Samsung Galaxy Ring, it provides me with additional health data in a less intrusive way especially for sleep where I find wearing watches unconformable. It is the first version of the product so there is definitely room for improvement moving forward.

Quality - the material feels relatively strong yet at the same time it feels cheap, if you order the sizing kit they literally feel the same as the plastic and you wouldn't be able to notice the different to the touch. The ring does feel slightly cheap when you can see the sensors through the ring when you look down it which does make it feel like it would be weaker. Given this I am yet to test the water resistance as I do not think it would hold up (so I remove for washing hands, in the shower, etc.)

Battery - I have been very impressed with the battery life, yet to dip below 80% as I put it in the charger whilst showering. These small charges here and there keep the charge high, given I have manually set the sensors to take constant readings (every 10 minutes). The charge case does feel very premium and is easy to have in a bag or pocket.

Health - The health tracking features have been very good so far, mainly the sleep tracking is very impressive - seeing HR, body temperature, etc throughout the night totalling into a sleep score and energy score is quite impressive. I have noticed that the step counter either highly over or under counts vs a smart watch - this is most likely something that can be fixed with a software update.

Overall I am impressed so far with the health features and the ability to track sleep in a more ergonomic manner. I do think the quality is lacking and I would not be inclined to recommend the product at the high price, given it is a first version I would advise possible buyers to wait for the second version which will take learnings from this, unless you want a product to track sleep in a nicer way vs a smart watch.
review.headline: Good but room for improvement

I don't always like wearing big bulky, smart watches, especially to bed. So I'm excited to get some sleep tracking in a different way through this ring and in addition to the sleep tracking, we also just have our general health metrics. Galaxy ring it is really nice to you can get some basic tracking metrics from just the smart ring. Don't need a smart watch if you can get your heart rate your work out duration. Your number of steps and also has your different heart rate zones and things so actually pretty in depth for A little ring here on my finger, but I think the ring would have definitely used more battery if I was tracking multiple workouts throughout the day, so samsung needs to work a bit on energy consumption.
review.headline: Almost perfect

review.reviewBody:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I ordered a ring sizing kit & was unsure between 8 & 9 so wore both for a full day & night on my index fingers....one felt a tad uncomfortable by morning & almost got stuck!
Panic over; larger size ordered!
When the ring arrived I was impressed by the premium packaging - black, sleek, sexy! 
The ring itself was in a clear plastic box which looked very sophisticated - this box is actually a charging dock for the ring. 
Now onto the actual ring.
It is nice to look at, not too bulky & feels comfortable to wear.
It was incredibly easy to set up, ready to go in minutes.
After day one I was excited to check my app to see what the Samsung Health app had to tell me.
So the ring tracks steps, active minutes and calories burnt. It does so in a simple way by providing data in number form but also by showing your "rings" (on this app hearts, which is cute) and therefore allowing you to see if you are on target & if not then how close you are to closing those rings, I.e hitting targets.
The ring tracks your sleep score & it does so in a completely non intrusive way as you really don't even notice you are wearing the ring. The app then gives explanations about the different stages of sleep & the importance of them before giving a breakdown of how long you were in each stage and whether or not this is sufficient.  I learned that I don't get enough sleep & I certainly don't spend enough of that time in mental recovery...this explains a lot -  the watch I was using previously was extremely unreliable when it came to sleep tracking.

You can also track your workouts, I have connected Fit and Strava so it pulls the information over automatically for me which makes it seamless and effortless on my part. I do wish Centr fed directly into it rather then me having to piggyback that info via another app.
Food tracking is also available. I've never really utilised something like this but thought Id try it out, it is a bit time consuming to add everything in but it was interesting to see the end result & honestly I can see how this would be helpful in my journey to a healthier lifestyle. 
Alongside food tracking you can also track water intake & set reminders to drink too.
It also tracks your cycle, a feature I've not seen on any other wearable & one that is highly welcomed!
Enjoying this wearable & looking forward to a more detailed insight into my health!

However I'm disappointed that after just two days my ring is scratched, I would expect it to be more hard-wearing.
review.headline: Closing those rings - on your ring!
